title: Immutable snapshots for concurrent readers
summary: Publish a whole replacement table and let readers retain a consistent older snapshot across later writes.
triggers: read-mostly shared state and copy-on-write snapshots
let readers keep a consistent view after releasing a shared mutex
prompts: Replace a routing table while active requests retain the exact version they started with.
Build the replacement table outside the mutex and publish it without exposing a partially updated map.
invariant: Each reader copies the pointer under the mutex and owns one immutable table. Publishing a replacement cannot invalidate that table.
mantra: Build outside the lock, publish once, read an owned snapshot.
pitfalls: Reference counting keeps the snapshot alive. The mutex protects the shared pointer member when a caller copies or replaces it.
The latest replacement wins. Building a replacement by editing an old snapshot can lose another writer’s changes without a revision check.
Long-lived readers keep older tables alive. Holding only a reference into a released snapshot can leave a dangling reference.
